tasks.title: Comparing Plants
tasks.reason: All notebook values are supplied to init; compare_plants answers deductions from that fixed input. No contestant calls to a hidden-state oracle or separate information channel.

tasks.title: Connecting Supertrees
tasks.reason: The complete path-count matrix is supplied. build only reports a construction and returns no hidden information.

tasks.title: Carnival Tickets
tasks.reason: All ticket values are supplied together. allocate_tickets reports the chosen allocation without feedback; the adversarial story is an optimization objective, not grader interrogation.

tasks.title: Packing Biscuits
tasks.reason: Each count_tastiness call receives the complete scenario and returns a count. There is no oracle or separated encoder/decoder.

tasks.title: Counting Mushrooms
tasks.reason: Hidden species are learned through use_machine feedback with a query budget; the official grader may adapt to previous queries.

tasks.title: Stations
tasks.reason: The first run encodes the full tree into bounded labels. A separate run routes using only local/target/neighbour labels and cannot reuse global state from the first run. No hidden-state query oracle is provided.

tasks.title: Nile
tasks.reason: All weights, costs and query parameters are supplied to one calculation function, which returns the answers. There is no hidden-state oracle or separated sender/receiver.

tasks.title: Message
tasks.reason: Separate sender and receiver programs transfer a message across a corrupted channel. The sender receives channel feedback. This establishes communication format rather than inferring it from a grader API.

tasks.title: Tree
tasks.reason: Initialization supplies the full tree and weights; later calls supply complete query parameters. Grader calls to init/query are not hidden-state interrogation or an encoding channel.

tasks.title: Hieroglyphs
tasks.reason: Both complete sequences are supplied and the function returns their universal common subsequence or failure. No interactive oracle or communication protocol is part of the interface.

tasks.title: Mosaic
tasks.reason: The boundary arrays and all rectangle queries are supplied together and a vector of answers is returned. The story's questions do not make the task interactive.

tasks.title: Sphinx's Riddle
tasks.reason: Vertex colours are hidden. The program chooses recolouring experiments and receives component counts to recover those colours within a query budget. There is no separate sender/receiver encoding task.

tasks.title: Number of Zeros
tasks.reason: The interval endpoints are given in standard input and one trailing-zero count is printed; no adaptive queries or separated encoder/decoder.

tasks.title: Luna Likes Love
tasks.reason: The full paired sequence is given and the minimum number of actions is printed. Story actions are not feedback from a grader.

tasks.title: Twin Cookies
tasks.reason: The program chooses cookie orders and receives one arbitrarily selected delivered value after each order; the grader may adapt. This is feedback interaction, not a separate encoder/decoder communication task.

tasks.title: Lanterns
tasks.reason: All heights and lantern specifications are supplied; print independently optimized costs. No oracle interaction or information-transfer protocol.

tasks.title: Shopping Fever
tasks.reason: All prices and the discount are supplied; output the optimum total. Transactions in the story are not exchanges with a judge.

tasks.title: Railway
tasks.reason: The full tunnels and timetables are supplied; output whether a collision occurs. No hidden feedback.

tasks.title: Angry Cows
tasks.reason: The entire weighted graph and area types are supplied; output an admissible optimum wall set or failure. No queries to recover unknown input.

tasks.title: Double Move
tasks.reason: Given a fixed game prefix, output counts of winning scenarios under optimal future play. Despite the game story, the contestant does not play interactively against the grader.
